title: Microsoft Purview: collection policies can filter Insider Risk Management device signals
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents PowerShell commands for creating and modifying collection policies, including a device-policy example, contrary to the briefing's portal-only guidance. The device scope also needs its documented Windows qualification, and the statement that no other control has a documented path is incorrect.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].governs; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A configured and deployed device collection policy takes precedence when its filtering conflicts with what an IRM policy monitors.
claims.quote: When a device collection policy is configured and deployed, if there's a conflict between what the Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor and what the collection policy is configured to filter for, the collection policy configuration takes precedence.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An activity filtered out by the collection policy is not collected or available for review in IRM, so IRM receives no signal for that activity.
claims.quote: if an Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor a specific activity, but the collection policy is configured to filter out that activity, the activity isn't collected and isn't available for review in Insider Risk Management.

claims.claim: IRM ignores a collected indicator for which its policy is not configured.
claims.quote: If a collection policy is configured to collect something that an Insider Risk Management policy isn't configured for, then the indicator is collected, but Insider Risk Management ignores it.

claims.claim: This precedence effect applies only to device indicators in IRM policies.
claims.quote: This only applies to device indicators in Insider Risk Management policies

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented IRM effect applies only when a device collection policy is deployed.
claims.quote: and only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Purview combines all collection policies for a data source into one policy during evaluation.
claims.quote: on the back end, during policy evaluation, Microsoft Purview combines all the collection policies for a data source into a single collection policy for that data source. So all the conditions for a data source are used when identifying matches.

claims.claim: Nothing in the IRM policy itself shows why a collection policy has filtered an activity out.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Insider risk management collection policy device indicators mismatch warning alert policy health'; opened the collection policies overview, policy indicators page and Create and manage Insider Risk Management policies, including its Policy health notification table.
claims.fix: Remove 'and nothing in the IRM policy itself shows why'. The sources do not establish what the UI can never display; the narrower documentation gap is already covered in Open questions.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or PowerShell for creating or changing collection policies, so changes must go through the portal.
claims.quote: Use the New-FeatureConfiguration cmdlet to create Microsoft Purview feature configurations within your organization, including: - Collection policies. ... This example creates a disabled collection policy named "Scoped collection policies for browser and devices"
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api with kind 'powershell', call 'New-FeatureConfiguration -Name <name> -FeatureScenario KnowYourData -Mode Enable -ScenarioConfig <configuration-json> -Locations <locations-json>', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-featureconfiguration?view=exchange-ps. Add to the note: 'Security & Compliance PowerShell; Public Preview, not available in all organizations. ScenarioConfig sets Activities and EnforcementPlanes; the device example uses Devices and an EndpointDevices location in Locations.' Replace the portal-only prose with 'Microsoft documents New-FeatureConfiguration for creating collection policies and Set-FeatureConfiguration for modifying them in Security & Compliance PowerShell. These cmdlets are Public Preview and are not available in all organizations.' Cite the New reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-featureconfiguration?view=exchange-ps.
